entries.title: A crew member who should be dead, moving wrong
Security drones still running their last order
A pack of eyeless things in the vents
Something huge that is only partly here
Radiation bleeding from a cracked reactor

entries.eldritch: The passage unspools before you at angles no shipwright ever drafted, each bulkhead older than the last, and you understand with a cold and sinking certainty that it is not growing longer. You are being let further in.
entries.plain: The corridor runs forty meters to a sealed hatch. You look again. Sixty.
entries.title: A corridor that is longer each time you look
entries.uneasy: The corridor keeps going. The deck plates repeat: the same scuff, the same missing bolt, as if the ship is running out of ideas.

entries.title: Black ice on the outer hull, stars below
A locked terminal holding a crew log
A glyph-door that matches the TOME's surface
A medical bay with one working pod
A navigation core that shows a place that is not on any chart
A survivor begging to be taken with you
A child's voice on the comms, repeating your name
A body arranged as an offering to the TOME
A rival Bearer who offers a trade
A memory from before you held the TOME, played back wrong
The TOME asks you to leave someone behind

entries.cleared: The iris grinds open with a sound like a sigh, and stale air rolls out to meet you.
entries.clue: Scratches on the iris are fresh, made from this side. Someone tried to get out, not in.
entries.eldritch: The docking iris hangs half-closed, its petals curled inward like the jaw of some leviathan that died mid-bite, and graven across them in a frantic, sleepless hand is a single word, LISTEN, which you find you are already doing, though you cannot say to what.
entries.plain: A docking iris frozen half-shut, its petals bent inward like broken teeth. Someone has scratched a word into it: LISTEN.
entries.title: The jammed iris door
entries.uneasy: The iris is frozen half-shut, its petals bent inward like teeth that closed on something and kept it. LISTEN, scratched into the metal. The word is cut deeper each time you look at it.

entries.clue: The blankets are arranged so the sleeper faces the door. Whoever lives here doesn't sleep much.
entries.eldritch: Amid ransacked shelves, where hungry fingers have flayed every seal, a single lamp keeps its feeble vigil over a burrow of blankets, and from behind a lifted wrench a woman regards you with the flat, unhallowed patience of one who has spent forty nights deciding what is real.
entries.plain: Shelves of sealed rations, most torn open by hands, not tools. A work lamp still burns low in the corner, guarding a nest of blankets. A woman in an engineer's jacket watches you over a raised wrench.
entries.title: The Ration Vault
entries.uneasy: Shelves of rations torn open by hands, not tools, all of them torn the same way. A work lamp burns low over a nest of blankets. A woman in an engineer's jacket watches you over a raised wrench, and she does not blink as often as she should.

entries.cleared: The drone spins, sparks, and drops dead on the deck.
entries.eldritch: A drone of the maintenance caste is flensing the copper sinews from the walls, and when it turns its blank optic upon you it ceases all motion, as a thing ceases that has been told by something larger to watch.
entries.plain: A maintenance drone with a cutting arm, stripping copper from the walls. It stops when it sees you.
entries.title: A scavenger drone
entries.uneasy: A maintenance drone strips copper from the walls with a cutting arm. It stops when it sees you, and holds still in a way machines do not usually bother to.

entries.cleared: You find the air handler's rhythm and slip through between its breaths.
entries.clue: Someone fed the plants with the station's distress beacon battery. They wanted the light more than the rescue.
entries.eldritch: The hydroponics bay has drowned in a black and stagnant tide, and over the racks there spreads a pallid, fleshlike bloom whose spores go wandering through the air in slow procession, every one of them, you are certain, drifting toward the door behind you.
entries.plain: The hydroponics bay is ankle-deep in black water. Pale fungus has swallowed the grow racks, and spore clouds drift like slow ghosts toward the door you came in by.
entries.title: Drowned Hydroponics
entries.uneasy: Black water to the ankle. The fungus on the grow racks is pale as skin, and the spore clouds drift toward the door you came in by, as if they heard it open.

entries.cleared: You understand at last: they're listening, not sleeping. You stop making noise worth hearing.
entries.clue: A duty roster on the wall: every name crossed out except E. VOSS and M. HALE.
entries.eldritch: Beneath a ceiling pressed low as a coffin lid the crew lie in their ranks, warm as the living and smiling as no living face has smiled, and in that close, breath-sour air you grasp with mounting dread that their stillness is not repose but attention.
entries.plain: Crew quarters. Forty bunks, forty occupants, none breathing. Room temperature is 31 degrees, eight above setting.
entries.title: Crew Quarters
entries.uneasy: Rows of bunks under a low ceiling. The air is warm and smells like breath. Every bunk is occupied. Every sleeper is smiling. None of them are breathing.

entries.cleared: The warden lowers the shotgun an inch. It is the most he will give you.
entries.clue: The static on the screen isn't random. It's a recording of a voice, slowed down thousands of times.
entries.eldritch: One screen alone among the dead still glows, and upon it the static heaves in long, oceanic swells, and before it sits a warden with a shotgun laid across his knees like a sacrament, keeping a watch he has plainly kept for longer than any man ought.
entries.plain: Banks of dead monitors and one live one, showing static that moves like a slow tide. A man in a warden's coat sits with a shotgun across his knees, watching it.
entries.title: The Signal Room
entries.uneasy: Dead monitors and one live one, its static moving like a slow tide. A man in a warden's coat watches it with a shotgun across his knees. He has not looked away from it, and he does not look away now.

entries.cleared: The turret's eye flickers, confused, and droops toward the floor.
entries.eldritch: From the vaulted dark a turret swings to follow you, its servos keening, and the thin red thread of its gaze slides across the deck to find you a heartbeat before you have decided where to step.
entries.plain: A ceiling turret tracks you with a whine of servos. Its targeting laser is the only other light here.
entries.title: The warden turret
entries.uneasy: A ceiling turret tracks you with a whine of servos. Its laser is the only other light, and it moves a fraction before you do.

entries.cleared: You haul yourself hand over hand past the breach, and an emergency shutter slams behind you.
entries.clue: The breach was cut from inside. Someone wanted this corridor to be hard to cross.
entries.eldritch: The station's spine runs a full league of shadow through its heart, and where a plate of the hull has peeled away the corridor shrieks its air into the abyss in a cadence so like breathing that you cannot shake the thought that the station is exhaling, and has been for forty days.
entries.plain: The station's spine runs a kilometer straight through its heart. A hull plate has peeled back, and the corridor howls as the station bleeds air into the black.
entries.title: The Spine
entries.uneasy: The spine runs a kilometer through the station. A hull plate has peeled back like a fingernail, and the corridor howls, and the howl has a rhythm to it, almost a breath.

entries.cleared: The Cantor's song breaks mid-note. The silence afterward is almost worse.
entries.clue: Hymn sheets on the chairs are station maintenance logs, with every mention of the lamp underlined.
entries.eldritch: The observation lounge is a chapel now, its pews arrayed before a window onto lightless nothing, and there a crewman in a faceplate daubed with black conducts an antediluvian hymn whose melody you cannot hear and yet, to your horror, already know.
entries.notes: App id: choir_cantor, renamed hymn_cantor per the lore notes.
entries.plain: The observation lounge has become a chapel: chairs in rows, facing a viewport of perfect black. A crewman in a pressure suit, faceplate painted black, conducts a hymn only the static can hear.
entries.title: The Cantor
entries.uneasy: The lounge has become a chapel: chairs in rows, facing a viewport of perfect black. A crewman with a painted-black faceplate conducts a hymn. You can't hear it, but your jaw aches as if you've been humming.

entries.cleared: The pod hums awake under your hands.
entries.clue: The medical log: Dr. Ilse Maren treated 'auditory contagion' for nine days, then wrote only one word, over and over: SING.
entries.eldritch: Alone in all that ruin the medical bay gleams immaculate, scoured to a surgical purity that is itself a kind of madness, and upon its screen the physician's log lies open to a final page where one word repeats until the words become a wall.
entries.plain: Clean. Shockingly clean. The medical bay's emergency lights still glow, and one pod still holds a charge. The medical log is open on the screen.
entries.title: Medical Bay
entries.uneasy: The medical bay is clean. Too clean, as if scrubbed again and again. One pod still holds a charge, and the log on the screen is open to the last page, waiting.

entries.cleared: You time the vents and cross, frost cracking off your shoulders.
entries.clue: The reactor's output has been rerouted, all of it, to the lamp. It's trying to relight itself.
entries.eldritch: The reactor broods in its pit below the catwalks, and from riven conduits the supercooled breath of the machine rolls out in shrieking cerements of white, timed with a deliberation that no mere failure of pressure could account for.
entries.plain: Catwalks hang over the reactor's sullen glow. Ruptured lines vent supercooled vapor in shrieking white sheets across the gallery.
entries.title: Reactor Gallery
entries.uneasy: Catwalks over the reactor's sullen glow. Ruptured lines vent supercooled vapor in white sheets, always in the same order, as if the gallery is breathing through its teeth.

entries.cleared: You turn the TOME toward the lens and the silhouette folds away into nothing.
entries.clue: There is a hollow in the great lens the exact shape of the slab you carry.
entries.eldritch: The lamp room rises about you like a cathedral raised by drowned shipwrights, all brass and cyclopean glass, and within the vast dark lens there stands a shape that is not a shape but an absence, a door of starless night in the form of a man, and it has been waiting for the light you carry.
entries.plain: Lamp room. Lens three stories tall, unlit. One figure standing inside it. No heat signature.
entries.title: The Dead Lamp
entries.uneasy: The lamp room is a cathedral of brass and glass, ringed around a lens three stories tall. It is completely dark, and something stands inside it, a silhouette cut out of the stars.

entries.cleared: The last drone's chord dies to a whimper of feedback.
entries.clue: One quarantine door has no name. It has a fresh lock and an empty cot. It's been waiting for someone.
entries.eldritch: Down a corridor shrouded in sheeting and sealed with names, the drones come seething from the vents, and from every speaker issues a single held chord, impossibly sustained, which bends by slow degrees toward the very note your own body makes.
entries.plain: Plastic sheeting, hazard tape, sealed doors with names on them. Drones crawl from the vents, their speakers humming one sustained, impossible chord.
entries.title: Quarantine Deck
entries.uneasy: Plastic sheeting, hazard tape, sealed doors with names on them. Drones crawl from the vents humming one sustained chord, and the chord is a little closer to your own pitch each time it starts again.

entries.cleared: The rows break and scatter like smoke, and the hangar is just a hangar again.
entries.clue: The shuttles have been gutted for their lights. Every bulb, every lamp, every screen.
entries.eldritch: Among the frost-rimed hulks of the shuttles stand the crew in silent rank upon rank, swaying all as one to some vast, tidal measure beyond hearing, and you know with a chill certainty that if you were to stand still among them long enough, you would begin to sway too.
entries.plain: Hangar bay. Shuttles in cradles, gutted. Twenty to thirty figures in uniform standing between them, swaying. None respond to hails.
entries.title: Hangar of Ghosts
entries.uneasy: Dead shuttles in their cradles, frost on every surface. Figures in uniform stand in rows between them, swaying in time to nothing.

entries.cleared: You slam the emergency brake and the lift shudders to a stop a meter above the floor.
entries.clue: Scratched into the lift wall: SHE KEEPS THE LAST ONE. SHE WON'T LET IT GO DARK.
entries.eldritch: The lift plunges in sickening, shuddering lurches, its brakes keening against the rails like a choir of the damned, and the floor count on its panel descends past the station's lowest deck into numbers that no blueprint ever held.
entries.plain: The cargo lift is the only way down to the lifeboats. It drops in sickening lurches, its brakes screaming against the rails.
entries.title: The Long Drop
entries.uneasy: The cargo lift drops in lurches, brakes screaming on the rails. The count of floors on the panel goes down, and down, and then down past numbers the station doesn't have.

entries.cleared: You stop listening. The whispers lose interest.
entries.eldritch: From every grille and speaker in the hull your name comes whispered, staggered like an echo running backward, and one voice among them speaks it a breath too early, with the dreadful familiarity of something that has been practising.
entries.plain: Every speaker in reach starts whispering your name, out of sync.
entries.title: The whisper static
entries.uneasy: Every speaker in reach whispers your name, out of sync. One of them is a half-second ahead of the others, as if it knows what the others are about to say.

entries.cleared: Gravity snaps back. You land on your feet, barely.
entries.eldritch: The station's gravity falters, and the world inverts, and you hang for one unmeasurable instant in a geometry where up and down are mere opinions held by things far older than the floor.
entries.plain: The artificial gravity stutters, and the floor becomes the ceiling for one long second.
entries.title: A gravity hiccup
entries.uneasy: The gravity stutters. For one long second the floor is the ceiling, and the second is longer than a second should be.
